title.narrative: IFCA contribution to the “Kyrgyzstan Sustainable Energy Efficiency Financing Facility - Extension (KyrSEFF II)”

description.narrative: KyrSEFF II will follow the initial pilot project with the following objectives:Develop climate finance capacities and project-oriented skills among PFIs; Provide effective support for (i) improving the capacity of financial intermediaries to appraise and finance resource efficiency, climate adaptation and small renewable energy investment projects and (ii) supporting local professionals to improve their technical expertise to identify and prepare technically feasible and bankable projects

description.narrative: Number of dedicated water efficiency subprojects financed (custom Indicator 2:)

comment.narrative: As of the end of Facility implementation KyrSEFF II has financed 41 subprojects in water efficiency in the agricultural and hospitality sectors supporting technologies such as drip irrigation water capture and storage water saving taps and facilities in guesthouses schools and wastewater treatment. On treegrown fruit the yield increase resulting from drip irrigation was between 2630. Regarding profitability consider a water cost reduction of up to 18 plus labour cost reduction drip irrigation requires minimal labour input and combine it with the yield increase to assume the profitability increase. The investments are expected to help save more than 166279 cubic metres of water a year and considering most subprojects are in rural areas will deliver significant impact the livelihood of beneficiaries.

comment.narrative: 808 Male 400 495 Female 408 505Tailored support and training was provided to each PFI for subproject origination activities in particular identifying the most promising technologies in each PFIs target sectors and for their clients. Results of this support are as follows 808 loan officers from six PFIs were trained. Facetoface meetings such as training and consultations were reduced and replaced with online meeting via Zoom. Since the beginning of pandemic there were no inperson capacity building sessions for loan officers. Support to the loan officers or groups of loan officers and other consultations were instead provided via email and by phone.
